open_points.subject: judge_execution / ExecutionObservation.report
open_points.text: - ExecutionObservation fields (exact, no others exist): timed_out: bool, exited_abnormally: bool, cleanup_confirmed: bool, wall_time_ms: int, memory_bytes: int, report: RunnerReport
open_points.other_text: - judge_execution: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] When cleanup was confirmed the outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit; sandbox_violation when the report holds any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value and spool ceilings are applied by the module that stores or spools an output.
open_points.question: How can judge_execution observe that no returned message was read when ExecutionObservation requires a non-optional RunnerReport and has no field representing an absent message; must report become optional or must the no-message condition be represented by another declared field?
